question_text: A 27-year-old male presents to the emergency department after being brought in from a house fire. The patient has extensive burns covering his body and is conscious but in severe pain. The patient has a past medical history notable for marijuana use. He is not currently on any medications. Physical exam is notable for extensive burns covering the patients back, chest, thighs, and legs. The patient's oropharynx reveals no signs of damage or extensive smoke inhalation. The patient is breathing on his own and has normal breath sounds bilaterally. His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), pulse is 145/min, blood pressure is 100/70 mmHg, respirations are 27/min, and oxygen saturation is 93% on room air. Which of the following interventions is most likely to reduce mortality in this patient?
